caption_hook: 🐢 Giant tortoises bounced back from under 1,000 to about 183,000, a 99-year-old flew on a plane's wing, and 6 more wins from this week 👇
question: Which win made your week? Reply with its number, 1 to 8 👇
share_line: Save this for a day you need hope
first_comment: This week's picks span the Seychelles, Egypt, England, deep space, India, South Korea, Switzerland and the USA. Which country should we feature more? 🌍

stories.headline: Hunted to under 1,000, giant tortoises now outnumber people
stories.summary: 19th-century hunting left fewer than 1,000 tortoises on Aldabra. After decades of protection, a new count estimates about 183,000 grown tortoises, more than the Seychelles' whole human population.
stories.why: Proof that protecting a place for decades can bring a species all the way back.

stories.stat_label: how tall the bigger statue once stood
stories.headline: A man working his land found 2 giant Ramesses II statues
stories.summary: Khaled el-Shahat found the statues in his village and called in experts. The bigger one once stood about 8.5 m tall; its head alone is 1.6 m and wears the double crown of Egypt.
stories.why: Ramesses II ruled for 66 years, one of the longest reigns in Egypt's history.

stories.stat_label: years old, the oldest wing-walker ever
stories.headline: At 99, she became the world's oldest wing-walker
stories.summary: Retired nurse Helga Duffy was strapped to the top of a small plane and flew for over 5 minutes, about 1,000 m up. Guinness confirmed the record, 3 months after a 97-year-old set it.
stories.why: Her niece saw the last record on the news and thought: Helga could do that.

stories.headline: Astronomers found the 1st green star ever seen
stories.summary: White dwarf WD J1330+6435 swallowed rocky debris from its old planets. Sodium in its dense atmosphere absorbs orange light, so to human eyes it would glow a ghostly green.
stories.why: No star, living or dead, had ever been credibly reported as green.

stories.stat_label: he held her head above water
stories.headline: An auto driver held a woman above water in a well for an hour
stories.summary: Pappachan Konoor was delivering a framed photo when a neighbour fell into a 16-foot well. He climbed in and kept her afloat for nearly an hour until firefighters pulled them out.
stories.why: The photo frame wasn't ready a day earlier. Because of that delay, he was there.

stories.headline: After 7 years of care, a rescued sea turtle goes home
stories.summary: Found on a Jeju beach in 2019, its shoulder and throat hurt by fishing gear, the loggerhead needed 7 surgeries at Aqua Planet Jeju. Now healthy, it returns to the sea near where it was found.
stories.why: Loggerheads are vulnerable, so every one returned to the ocean counts.

stories.headline: A gene therapy helped blind patients find objects again
stories.summary: In a trial for advanced retinitis pigmentosa, one injection made surviving eye cells sense light. With special goggles, 7 of 10 patients saw more light, and some found doors and objects.
stories.why: It works whatever the faulty gene, so one approach could help many forms of blindness.

stories.headline: A wildlife bridge cut animal crashes on a highway by 91%
stories.summary: Drivers once hit an animal about once a day on this stretch of I-25. In the 10 months since North America's largest wildlife overpass opened, they have hit just 2.
stories.why: Elk, bears and even frogs now cross safely, and a pronghorn crossed for the 1st time in decades.

fun_fact: Aldabra giant tortoises can live for well over 100 years.
